title: Correction to: Exact semidefinite formulations for a class of (random and non-random) nonconvex quadratic programs
contribution: Withdraws Theorem 3 of Burer & Ye (2020) by proving that the systems its proof needed can never be simultaneously feasible, and replaces it with a geometric sufficient condition (int(K_j) meets L_j at every vertex of conv{f_j}) and a high-probability Shor-exactness theorem for random diagonal QCQPs with fixed m.
problem_entry: An error reported by Kilinc-Karzan and Wang is located in the analysis of system (12) in the proof of Theorem 3, and it is shown to be fatal: the probability that all systems are feasible is zero (p. 1).
key_idea: Map each variable j of a diagonal QCQP to a point f_j and a direction d_j in R^{1+m}; the Shor SDP is exact (r* = 1) if the line spanned by d_j meets the interior of the cone of feasible directions K_j at f_j in conv{f_1..f_n} for every j, which holds with probability tending to 1 for sphere-uniform f_j and angle-bounded d_j (pp. 2-3).
assumptions: Diagonal QCQP (1) under S019's Assumptions 1-3 with a redundant ball x^T x <= rho^2 (rho not needed explicitly); random model with m and theta fixed, f_j/||f_j|| uniform on the sphere, angle between d_j and f_j outside pi/2 +- theta (pp. 2-3); scope explicitly narrowed to diagonal instances (p. 2).
proof_devices: zero-coefficient extreme: minimal omega with D_i + omega B_i PSD zeroes one diagonal entry, so the system with that variable free forces a nonnegative combination to be <= -omega (pp. 1-2)
sufficient restrictive subsystem with diagonal X; eliminate the free X_jj via I . X = 0 to get sum_{k != j} X_kk (f_k - f_j) + x_j d_j < 0 (p. 2)
geometric translation: feasibility iff K_j meets L_j + int(R_-^{1+m}), with int(L_j + R_-) = L_j + int(R_-) since L_j is a line (p. 3)
full-dimensionality/interior argument: int(K_j) meets L_j implies K_j meets int(L_j + R_-) (p. 3)
scale normalization x_j = xhat_j/||f_j||, justified because positive variable scalings do not affect Shor tightness (p. 3)
asymptotic geometry: Q approaches the unit ball and K_j approaches the halfspace {v: f_j^T v <= 0} as n -> infinity; stated qualitatively, no rate (p. 3)
experiments: none; the Remark gives a Gaussian plus accept-reject recipe for generating instances satisfying the theorem (p. 4), but no computation is reported
positioning: Pure repair of the original article [1] (only reference, p. 4); reuses its numbering and assumptions; finders named and thanked in the first paragraph (p. 1).
writing: Error stated in the first sentence, finders credited at once, failure explained as a zero-probability event ('Said differently'), old result called 'the purported Theorem 3', narrowing announced before the replacement statement (pp. 1-2); one interpretive sentence per geometric object (p. 2).
limits_future: Replacement covers only diagonal instances with fixed m and an angle condition on the linear terms; the limit argument is qualitative; whether the general random-QCQP claim is false or only unproved is not settled; the arXiv version is not mentioned; no future work stated (pp. 2-3).

method_links.note: Narrow publicly when wrong: error located (system (12)), shown fatal (probability zero), strongest provable special case kept (diagonal instances), finders thanked by name.
Step 7 (update every public version) is not addressed: the note says nothing about arXiv 1802.02688; the arXiv state was not checked in this batch.
The exactness hypothesis for the Shor SDP is rewritten as an explicit, picturable geometric condition (cone of feasible directions vs. a line at each vertex of conv{f_j}).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: refute by joint infeasibility, not by counterexample instance
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The flawed probabilistic proof is shown wrong because the systems it needs cannot be simultaneously feasible for any data, via a minimal-omega zero-coefficient argument; no instance search is needed.
Each variable becomes a point f_j and direction d_j in R^{1+m}; Shor exactness reduces to int(K_j) meeting L_j at every vertex of the polytope conv{f_j}.

transferable: Disprove a 'with high probability all systems are feasible' step by picking the extreme multiplier (minimal omega with D_i + omega B_i PSD) that zeroes one coefficient, then show the system in which that variable is free forces a nonnegative combination to be negative (pp. 1-2).

For a separable QCQP, encode each variable's coefficients as a point f_j and direction d_j in R^{1+m}; n LP feasibility systems then become cone-meets-line conditions at the vertices of conv{f_j} (pp. 2-3).
Use an invariance of the property (positive variable scaling preserves Shor tightness) to normalize random data onto the unit sphere before the asymptotic argument (p. 3).
In a correction note: error in the first sentence, finders credited in the same paragraph, proof that the old route cannot be repaired, narrowing announced before the replacement statement (pp. 1-2).

quotes.text: However, in truth the proof fails because, with this setup, the systems cannot be simultaneously feasible.
Instead of the purported Theorem 3, we now prove an analogous theorem, except that it only applies to diagonal instances of (1).
